figures.before: Tilt-Up Concrete Construction: What It Is and How It Works
figures.alt: Tilt-up warehouse shell with tall concrete panels, temporary braces, finished slab, and staged roof joists
figures.caption: Tilt-up construction joins the slab, panel casting, erection sequence, temporary bracing, roof structure, and exterior enclosure into a single coordinated shell package.

figures.before: Pre-Engineered Steel Frame Construction: What It Is and How It Works
figures.alt: Pre-engineered steel warehouse frame under construction with rigid frames, roof purlins, bracing, and concrete foundations
figures.caption: A steel-frame warehouse is driven by the frame grid, foundations, bracing, roof and wall systems, openings, and the fabrication sequence that brings the shell together.

figures.alt: Pre-engineered metal building erection with rigid steel frames, base plates, anchor bolts, purlins, bracing, and concrete foundations
figures.caption: Cost comparisons need to include more than the structural frame. Foundations, envelope, schedule, crane or erection needs, site work, fire protection, and tenant requirements all change the project result.
